title: 20: Fastbin Dup
desc: Fastbins are used for small chunks when the tcache is full. Fastbins only check if the chunk being freed is the same as the head of the list. By freeing A, then B, then A again, you bypass the check and create a cycle: A → B → A → B → ... This lets you get two allocations at the same address and control where the third one lands.
source: // Fill tcache (7 frees of same size)
for (int i=0; i<7; i++) t[i] = malloc(16);

log: Tcache is already full (7 entries for size 24). Chunks A and B are allocated.
free(a) — tcache is full, so A goes to the fastbin instead.
free(b) — B also goes to fastbin. Fastbin[24]: B → A → nil
free(a) AGAIN! Fastbin only checks if A == head. Head is B, so the check passes. Fastbin[24]: A → B → A → B → ... (cycle!)
Drain tcache with 7 mallocs so next mallocs come from fastbin.
The fastbin has a cycle. Write the target address to poison the fd pointer!

winMsg: Fastbin only checks if the chunk being freed is the same as the list head. By freeing B between two frees of A, you bypassed the check and created a cycle. This gave you two allocations at the same address — and control over where the third allocation lands.
